data_exchange_osrd_desc: An open source web application for railway infrastructure design, capacity analysis, timetabling and simulation
data_exchange_alignment_desc: Exchange format {{version}} – horizontal and vertical alignment per track, with every design parameter. Not OSRD RailJSON.
data_exchange_server_desc: Put the open project on open-layout-tool.org. Anyone may take it from there; putting it there needs the password. What is stored is public — do not upload anything confidential.

data_exchange_server_err_id_mismatch: Project does not match the server entry
data_exchange_server_err_not_configured: The server is not set up for this

data_exchange_server_err_no_data_dir: The server could not write the file

s_curve_no_result: Connection did not converge – check inputs.
info_description: This tool is for creating track geometry that can be used in an operational simulation. The data can currently be exported and used in OSRD.
info_layers: Switch the background map for a solid planning base – from OpenStreetMap maps to aerial imagery, terrain models and official state survey maps.
info_places: Plan new tracks that don't connect to existing infrastructure – as a straight line, a curve, or offset in parallel to an existing element or track.
info_connect: Extend existing tracks with new elements at the end node – straights or curves, with transition curves and cant where needed.
info_connect_switch: Place a new straight or curved switch, insert one into an existing track, across several straights, curves and clothoids if needed, or connect two parallel tracks with a calculated switch connection.
info_splice: Join two straights with an arc, or two arcs with a straight (including clothoids), for a smooth, continuous alignment.
info_edit: Select an element to adjust its length and radius or delete it, or a track to edit its properties, reverse its direction, open the table editor, or delete it.
info_optimize: Improve curve radii within a chosen offset corridor to raise the achievable speed – for a whole track or a single arc, with an optional global optimization (Python).
info_platform: Select a track and two points on it to lay out a platform – its edges follow the track at 1.67 m and 4.67 m from the axis, on the side you choose.
info_data: Import and export your data – as a project file, individual tracks, survey data, CSV, or via OSRD.
info_elevation: Select a track to see its elevation profile, and fill in missing heights automatically from the terrain model.
info_plan: Preview and export a scale plan (1:500/1:1000) as PDF, split across multiple sheets if needed – with title block, scale bar, north arrow and background map.
scurve_no_solution: No solution: the tracks meet at too sharp an angle.
scurve_too_short: Intermediate element shorter than the switch form's minimum.
scurve_too_sharp: Tracks converge too much: the intermediate curve is too sharp for this speed.
plan_intro: Creates a to-scale site plan of the tracks as a PDF.
plan_background_failed: Background map could not be loaded – plan without background.
plan_km_missing: No kilometrage line in the project – give a track a line number and it is fetched.
plan_legend: UA/UE transition start/end · BA/BE arc start/end · TA/TE alignment start/end · stations km+m
plan_overflow: The tracks do not fit on one sheet – switch on splitting, or pick a larger format or 1:1000.
platform_hint_track: Select the track the platform runs along on the map.
platform_hint_start: Click the start point of the platform on the track
platform_hint_end: Click the end point of the platform on the track
platform_error_range: Start and end must lie on the track and at least 1 m apart.
elevation_hint: Pick a track to see its profile. Tracks without heights get them automatically from the terrain (DGM5 of the BKG, MapTiler Terrain outside Germany); a track that grows only has the new stretch read. Heights edited by hand stay until the track is reloaded.
elevation_reload_track: Reload the track’s heights from the terrain
elevation_no_heights: No heights for this track yet.
elevation_hint_edit: Click a point to change its height. Ctrl/Shift-click picks more, Shift-drag draws a box. Wheel zooms, drag pans.
elevation_delete_hint: The first and the last point stay — that is where the height meets the joined tracks.
elevation_vcurve_hint: Radius of the vertical curve at the gradient change in m; 0 removes it.
